newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean shrs tumble; rates cut after market shuts.
newsitem.headline: Chilean shrs tumble; rates cut after market shuts.

text.p: Chilean stocks plunged nearly two points as a rush of overseas buying dried up on profit-taking and feelings the bourse had grown too expensive, brokers said.
Prices also fell on comments from a Central Bank board member that an interest rate cut was not imminent after all -- yet the Central Bank then cut rates after the market closed.

The blue-chip IPSA index tumbled 1.8 points to 130.87 points, reversing gains in a record-breaking rally, which ended Tuesday. The all-share IGPA index was off 0.79 percent to 5675.72 points in slow volume of 12 billion pesos.
In an unusual case of crossed signals, Central Bank board member Pablo Pinera said in London before the local market opened that he did not expect an interest cut soon.
His comments put more bearish pressure on prices, already on their way down over the past two days after a heady rally began in mid-May.

But barely half an hour after the market closed, the Central Bank did exactly what Pinera said it would not do. It cut the interbank rate by 25 basis points to 6.75 percent annual, a small reduction in line with what analysts had been forecasting.

Analysts saw a rate cut coming since Tuesday when the government announced that consumer prices rose 0.2 percent in May -- the smallest monthly rise since 1995 and practically guaranteeing fulfillment of the annual inflation goal of 5.5 percent, officials said.

Big-volume electrical shares, just recovered from the effects of drought on their dam water levels and share prices, were mostly down. Endesa was off 3.2 percent to 303 pesos, and Colbun was off 0.5 percent to 45.25 pesos.
"Prices go up high enough and certain people stop buying. The air went out of it," one broker said before the rate cut.

Power utility Chilgener ended down 0.3 percent to 171.50 pesos from Wednesday's close. After the market closed, Chilgener announced it bought 49 percent of Peru's Inversiones Dominion, which owns privatized utility Egenor -- effectively giving Chilgener its first stake in the Peruvian electricity industry.
Chilgener, the main competitor to the Enersis-Endesa group, already has major investments in power generators in Brazil, Colombia and Argentina.
